article.Citation/Title: Dakwar, E., Levin, F., Hart, C. L., Basaraba, C., Choi, J., Pavlicova, M., & Nunes, E. V. (2020). A single ketamine infusion combined with motivational enhancement therapy for alcohol use disorder: A randomized midazolam-controlled pilot trial. American Journal of Psychiatry, 177(2), 125-133.
article.InterventionDescription: Single 52-min IV ketamine infusion (0.71 mg/kg total) or midazolam (0.025 mg/kg) during week 2 of 5-week outpatient motivational enhancement therapy at a psychiatric research clinic.

ae_events.Description: Post-infusion sedation, most common adverse effect (ketamine N=8; midazolam comparator N=12).
Post-infusion headache, persisting about 12 hours (ketamine N=6; midazolam comparator N=4).
Significantly higher dissociative-state (CADSS) scores in ketamine vs. midazolam group immediately post-infusion; not associated with end-of-study abstinence.
Mild agitation in ketamine-group participants (N=2), lasting about 1 hour post-infusion.

article.Year: Article states 'published online Dec. 2, 2019' but the version-of-record issue header reads 'Am J Psychiatry 2020; 177:125-133' / 'Am J Psychiatry 177:2, February 2020'. Per the request's Year=2020 and the issue-year rule, 2020 (issue) is used; 2019 (online-first) is the noted discrepancy.
article.Outcome: Primary outcome is self-reported alcohol abstinence (dichotomized abstinent/nonabstinent days) over 21 days postinfusion, per the longitudinal logistic mixed-effects model (Methods 'Statistical Analysis'; Results 'Primary Outcome: Alcohol Abstinence'). The time-by-treatment interaction is the test of ketamine vs. midazolam on this primary outcome: F=25.1, df=1,797. Outcome is coded as the bare F value (25.1); the labelled statistic with df is carried in SD.
article.SD: Same sentence as Outcome ('Primary Outcome: Alcohol Abstinence' paragraph): 'the time-by-treatment interaction (F=25.1, df=1, 797, p,0.001)'. Reported as 'F(1,797) = 25.1' with df in parentheses as required.
article.PVal: Printed in the text as 'p,0.001' (Primary Outcome paragraph). The comma is a clear OCR/typographic substitution for '<' — the identical 'p,0.001' pattern recurs verbatim later in the Secondary Outcomes section for a different F-test, while a nearby correctly-rendered value in the same paragraph reads 'p=0.004'. Read through as '<0.001' per the instruction to read through unambiguous punctuation artifacts; this is a punctuation correction, not a fabricated number.
article.SampleSize_NFinal: N=40, the full randomized/intent-to-treat sample ('40 were randomly assigned in an intent-to-treat analysis', Results/Participants), consistent with the primary model using all randomized participants with missing days imputed as nonabstinent.

MethodologyDescribedYN.note: All 14 elements are explicitly described: objective (Abstract), design/setting (RCT at NY State Psychiatric Institute), eligibility (DSM-IV alcohol dependence + inclusion/exclusion list), intervention/comparator (ketamine vs. midazolam dosing detailed), outcomes (primary abstinence, secondary heavy-drinking/relapse), sample_size_power (target N=60 for adequate power to detect a large effect), randomization (1:1 statistician-generated random blocks), blinding (staff blinded; participant deception procedure), statistical_methods (detailed mixed-effects modeling section), results (fully reported with test statistics), harms (adverse-effects paragraph), funding_coi (NIAAA/NIDA grants listed; no commercial COI).

article.BaseStatus: No formal DSM-5 severity subtype or validated severity score (e.g., AUDIT) is reported. Coded 'Severe' by inference from the DSM-IV 'alcohol dependence' diagnosis (the more severe of the two DSM-IV categories) combined with the quantitative eligibility threshold (>=4 heavy drinking days/week or >=35/28 drinks/week) and observed baseline consumption (~5-6.6 drinks/day, Table 1). This is an inferential judgment rather than an author-assigned severity label.
article.Retention (%): Denominator = randomized N=40 (both randomized N=40 and enrolled N=50 are reported, so randomized is used). Completers: midazolam 23-6 dropouts=17; ketamine 17-0 dropouts=17 (CONSORT diagram, Figure 1; confirmed in Results/Participants: 'six participants dropped out of the midazolam group... No participants dropped out of the ketamine group'). Total completers=34/40=85%.
article.Double+Blind: Coded 1 from two passages: 'All staff involved in this trial were blinded to treatment condition' (Study Setting) and the deception procedure in which participants 'were informed that they might receive any of several medications, in addition to ketamine or midazolam... intended to disguise what drug was specifically given' (Infusion Procedures) — i.e., both participants and staff were nominally blinded by design. The Discussion explicitly notes blind integrity was never formally tested ('we did not test the integrity of the blind'), and ketamine's dissociative effects plausibly compromised it in practice; the code reflects design intent, not verified effectiveness.
article.MentalHealthChangeMeasured: Coded 1 because perceived stress and mindfulness were tracked longitudinally and modeled as secondary outcomes over time ('When modeling the secondary outcomes (craving, withdrawal, mindfulness, impulsivity, stress sensitivity, and self-efficacy)...', Secondary Outcomes). The Hamilton Depression Rating Scale, by contrast, appears only as a Table 1 baseline/exclusion measure, not a repeated outcome. Borderline call resting on the stress/mindfulness constructs rather than a canonical depression/anxiety endpoint.
article.Implementation Outcome: Coded 1 because treatment fidelity (an implementation outcome) was explicitly monitored and reported: 'fidelity to the motivational enhancement therapy manual was monitored through supervision and review of audiotaped sessions only' (Limitations).
article.Followup in months: Longest reported follow-up is the 6-month post-trial telephone interview (partial response: data collected for 19/40 = 47.5%; Results). This differs materially from the 21-day (~0.7-month) primary-outcome assessment window; both are reported, and the field captures the longer duration per the 'longest follow-up' rule.
article.RaceEthnicity_BIPOCPercent: Table 1: Asian 5.4% + Black or African American 13.5% + Multiracial 10.8% = 29.7% (consistent with White=70.3%; 100-70.3=29.7).
article.SocioeconomicStatusYN: No income, low-income eligibility, or public-insurance criteria are described anywhere in the article; only employment status is reported (71.8% employed), which does not meet the SES-description definition. Coded 0.
article.RecruitmentRepresentYN: Sample was treatment-seeking and heavily screened: 95 screened, 45 excluded pre-enrollment (31 did not meet criteria, 14 not interested/lost contact), plus exclusions for psychiatric/medical comorbidity, current depressive symptoms, and severe withdrawal history. Coded 0 as not representative of real-world community/clinical populations.
article.AE_denominator: 40 = sum of both randomized arms (ketamine N=17 + midazolam N=23), both of which received an infusion and were monitored for adverse effects (Results/Participants; CONSORT diagram).

ae_events.Dakwar 2020_AE01: Results/Participants paragraph reports sedation as the most common adverse effect, given per-arm (midazolam N=12; ketamine N=8). Ketamine-arm N=8 used for NAffected (ArmScope=psychedelic_arm); midazolam's N=12 is retained in Description for completeness rather than summed. Graded Mild: transient, no intervention or persistence noted, resolved ~12h postinfusion.
ae_events.Dakwar 2020_AE02: Same sentence as sedation. Ketamine-arm N=6 used for NAffected; midazolam N=4 noted in Description. Graded Mild: transient, resolved ~12h postinfusion, no intervention reported.
ae_events.Dakwar 2020_AE03: CADSS dissociative-state score comparison (median=19, IQR 9-30.75, ketamine vs. median=2, IQR 0.25-9.25, midazolam; chi2=7.87, p=0.005) is a measured/expected ketamine effect rather than an author-labeled adverse event, so it is coded AE_type=challenging_experience per the CEQ-phenomenology guidance rather than a clinical AE. NAffected is coded '.' because the article reports group medians/IQR, not a participant count meeting a threshold. Graded Mild per the rubric's core adaptation principle (a high dissociation score alone is Mild absent intervention need or persistence); the article separately states there were 'no incidents of persistent psychoactive effects' in either group.
ae_events.Dakwar 2020_AE04: Authors explicitly label the event 'mild agitation' (SeveritySource=author) in 2 ketamine-group participants, lasting about 1 hour postinfusion, with no intervention reported.

config_proposal.note: Primary outcome (21-day alcohol abstinence) tested via the time-by-treatment interaction, F(1,797)=25.1, p<.001 (single-numerator-df F, directly convertible to a Hedges' g equivalent); direction=1 because the effect favors ketamine, the psychedelic arm.
